# package batch

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus/batch"
```

Package batch plans, executes and decodes sets of Modbus reads.

A batch is a list of named read items. Compile validates the items and groups them into windows: the read requests that cover them, each within the protocol and device limits, never mixing unit IDs or address spaces. Items that are contiguous or overlap share a window; merging across unrequested addresses happens only when Options.MaxGap allows it.

A Plan is immutable and safe for concurrent use. It can be inspected without I/O (Windows, Stats, FunctionCodes). Execute reads its windows one after another through a Reader such as \*modbus.Client, and Decode turns captured window data into the same result: per-item results, with an explicit State for every window and item, kept when a batch fails part-way. The package does not schedule, cache, retry or start goroutines: a batch is planned once and run when the caller decides.

## Variables

```go
var ErrIncomplete = errors.New("batch: not every window was read")
```

ErrIncomplete is matched by the error of an Execute that did not read every window.

```go
var ErrNotAttempted = errors.New("batch: window not attempted")
```

ErrNotAttempted marks a window that was not read because the batch stopped before it. WindowResult.Err and ItemResult.Err wrap it for such windows.

### type ExecError

```go
type ExecError struct {

	// First is the error of the first Failed window, nil when none failed.
```

ExecError is the error of an Execute that did not read every window. It matches ErrIncomplete, its first window error and the reason the batch stopped, so errors.Is(err, modbus.ErrIllegalDataAddress) and errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) both work.

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// MaxGap is the number of unrequested registers or bits a window may
	// span between two items. Zero merges contiguous and overlapping items
	// only. Gaps are read, so a device must allow reads of those addresses.
	MaxGap uint16
	// MaxRegisters is the largest register window, 1..modbus.MaxReadRegisters.
	// Zero selects modbus.MaxReadRegisters.
	MaxRegisters uint16
	// MaxBits is the largest coil or discrete input window,
	// 1..modbus.MaxReadCoils. Zero selects modbus.MaxReadCoils.
	MaxBits uint16
	// Boundaries are addresses no window may span, for devices that reject
	// reads across internal blocks.
	Boundaries []Boundary
	// ContinueOnTransportError makes Execute go on with the next window
	// after a transport error (a timeout, a broken connection, a protocol
	// error) instead of ending the batch. A cancelled or expired context
	// always ends it. The planner ignores it.
	ContinueOnTransportError bool
}
```

Options configures how Compile groups items into windows. The zero value merges contiguous and overlapping items only, up to the protocol limits.

Plan is a compiled batch. It is immutable and safe for concurrent use.

#### func Compile

```go
func Compile(items []Item, opts Options) (*Plan, error)
```

Compile validates items and groups them into windows. It performs no I/O.

Items are grouped by unit ID and function code, and each group is swept in address order: an item joins the current window when it starts at most opts.MaxGap addresses after the window's end, the merged window stays within the limit and no boundary falls inside it. An item larger than the limit gets consecutive windows of its own. Windows are ordered by unit ID, function code and address, so the result does not depend on the order of items.

Compile returns a \*ValidationError for invalid options or items: an empty or duplicate name, a function code other than FC01-FC04, a codec on a bit item or with a count that disagrees with Count, a zero count, a range past address 0xFFFF, or an item that spans a boundary.

#### func (Plan) Decode

```go
func (p *Plan) Decode(data []WindowData) (*Result, error)
```

Decode builds the result of the plan from the data of its windows, one WindowData per window in Plan.Windows order: from a capture, or in tests.

A window whose data has no error must hold exactly its count of registers or bits; Decode returns a \*ValidationError otherwise, and for a data slice of the wrong length. A window error marks the window Failed, or NotAttempted when it wraps ErrNotAttempted.

#### func (Plan) Execute

```go
func (p *Plan) Execute(ctx context.Context, r Reader) (*Result, error)
```

Execute reads the plan's windows from r, in plan order, one request after another on the calling goroutine, and returns the result of every window and item. It starts no goroutines and keeps no state between calls, so a plan can be executed repeatedly and concurrently. Sequential requests are not an atomic snapshot: every window carries its own timing.

A Modbus exception, and a request the client refuses through modbus.Config.AllowedFunctionCodes, fail only that window; the batch goes on. Any other error (a timeout, a broken connection, a protocol error) ends the batch: the remaining windows are NotAttempted, unless Options.ContinueOnTransportError is set. A cancelled or expired context always ends the batch. Before each window the context is checked, and the in-flight request is cancelled through it.

The error is nil when every window is OK; an item whose codec rejects its registers is DecodeFailed and does not set it. Otherwise Execute returns the result together with an \*ExecError. A nil r returns a nil result and a \*ValidationError.

### type Result

```go
type Result struct {
	// Started and Finished bound the whole batch. Both are zero for a result
	// decoded offline.
	Started, Finished time.Time
	// Windows holds one result per window, in Plan.Windows order.
	Windows []WindowResult
	// Items holds one result per item, in Plan.Items order.
	Items []ItemResult
}
```

Result holds the outcome of every window and item of a plan. Slices in a Result may share storage with each other.

### type State

```go
type State uint8
```

State is the outcome of one window or one item. The zero value is NotAttempted.

```go
const (
	// NotAttempted: the window was not read, because the batch stopped or
	// was cancelled before it.
	NotAttempted State = iota
	// Failed: the request was made and failed.
	Failed
	// DecodeFailed: the item was read, but its codec rejected the
	// registers. Items only.
	DecodeFailed
	// OK: read, and decoded when the item has a codec.
	OK
)
```
